history: Named for the Broadway musical that opened in 1900, and served at the Waldorf-Astoria to its chorus. One of the earliest raspberry-and-ginger highballs on an American list.
whyItWorks: Raspberry is soft and ginger is sharp; lime sits between them and stops the fruit reading as syrup.
steps: Muddle the raspberries with the lime and syrup in the shaker.
Add the gin and ice and shake.
Double-strain into an ice-filled collins glass.
Top with ginger beer and stir once from the bottom.
techniqueNotes: The period recipe uses raspberry syrup; muddling fresh fruit gives a cleaner, less sweet drink.
Double-strain or you will be drinking seeds.

recommendedBottles.rationale: Holds its own against the ginger.

substitutions.notes: ¾ oz raspberry syrup in place of the fruit — the original build.
Ginger ale or soda makes it lighter and much less spicy.

name: Floradora
description: Gin, lime and muddled raspberries, lengthened with ginger beer.
